ramayana-3-15-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-22.translation: The rivers now shine with water hidden by mist, cranes known only by their calls, and banks of frost-wet sand.
ramayana-3-15-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-23.translation: Because of the frost, the weak sun and the cold, even water on a mountain top usually tastes good.
ramayana-3-15-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-24.translation: The lotus ponds, blasted by frost, their leaves withered with age and their filaments and seed pods fallen, with only stalks left, do not shine.
ramayana-3-15-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-25.translation: In this season, tiger among men, the righteous Bharata, full of sorrow, practises austerity in the city out of devotion to you.
ramayana-3-15-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-26.translation: Giving up the kingdom, honour and many pleasures, he lives as an ascetic, eats sparingly and sleeps on the cold ground.
ramayana-3-15-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-27.translation: He too, surely, at this hour, ready for his bath, goes to the Sarayu river, always surrounded by his people.
ramayana-3-15-27.meaning: Bharata too goes to bathe at dawn.
ramayana-3-15-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-28.translation: Raised in great comfort, delicate and pained by the cold, how does he plunge into the Sarayu in the last hours of the night?
ramayana-3-15-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-29.translation: Lotus-eyed, dark, glorious, slim-waisted, great, knowing dharma, truthful, restrained by modesty, master of his senses,
ramayana-3-15-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-30.translation: sweet-spoken, gentle, long-armed, subduer of foes, he has given up every comfort and taken refuge wholly in his noble brother.
ramayana-3-15-30.meaning: Bharata has given himself entirely to Rama.
ramayana-3-15-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-31.translation: Your great-souled brother Bharata has won heaven, for he follows you in austerity even while you live in the forest.
ramayana-3-15-31.meaning: Bharata's devotion is its own reward.
ramayana-3-15-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-32.translation: The saying goes that men take after their mother, not their father; Bharata has proved it wrong.
ramayana-3-15-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-33.translation: How could Kaikeyi, whose husband is Dasharatha and whose son is the good Bharata, be so cruel-minded?'
ramayana-3-15-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-34.translation: As righteous Lakshmana spoke these words out of love, Rama, not bearing that blame of their mother, said:
ramayana-3-15-34.meaning: Rama would not allow criticism of Kaikeyi.
ramayana-3-15-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-35.translation: 'Dear one, you must never speak ill of our middle mother. Speak only of Bharata, lord of the Ikshvakus.
ramayana-3-15-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi. Rama refuses to hold a grudge.

ramayana-3-15-36.translation: Though my mind is set firm on forest life, burning with love for Bharata it becomes weak again.'
ramayana-3-15-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-37.translation: Lamenting thus, Rama reached the Godavari and bathed with Lakshmana and Sita.
ramayana-3-15-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-38.translation: Then they offered water to the ancestors and gods and, composed, praised the rising sun and the deities.
ramayana-3-15-38.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-15-39.translation: Having bathed, Rama shone with Sita and Lakshmana, like the lord Rudra with Parvati, daughter of the mountain, and Nandi after bathing.
ramayana-3-15-39.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 15: winter arrives; walking to the Godavari, Lakshmana describes the season and speaks of Bharata's devotion, and Rama gently stops him from blaming Kaikeyi.

ramayana-3-16-1.translation: Having bathed, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana went from the bank of the Godavari to their hermitage.
ramayana-3-16-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-2.translation: Reaching the hermitage, Rama with Lakshmana performed the morning rites and went to the leaf hut.
ramayana-3-16-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-3.translation: Seated in the leaf hut with Sita, the mighty-armed Rama shone like the moon with the star Chitra, and talked of many things with his brother Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-16-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-4.translation: As Rama sat absorbed in conversation, a demoness happened to come to that place.
ramayana-3-16-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-5.translation: She was Shurpanakha, sister of the ten-headed demon Ravana; approaching Rama, she saw that he was like a god.
ramayana-3-16-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-6.translation: lion-chested, mighty-armed, with eyes like lotus petals, gentle, of great spirit, bearing the marks of a king,
ramayana-3-16-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-7.translation: Seeing Rama, dark as a blue lotus, shining like the god of love, like Indra, the demoness was overcome by desire.
ramayana-3-16-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-8.translation: He was fair-faced, she ugly-faced; he slim-waisted, she pot-bellied; he large-eyed, she with deformed eyes; he with lovely hair, she with copper-coloured hair;
ramayana-3-16-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-9.translation: he pleasing, she misshapen; he sweet-voiced, she harsh-voiced; he young, she old and fearsome; he courteous, she crooked in speech;
ramayana-3-16-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-10.translation: he upright in conduct, she very ill-behaved; he lovely, she unpleasant to look at. Possessed by desire, the demoness said to Rama:
ramayana-3-16-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-11.translation: 'With matted hair, in ascetic's form, with a wife and carrying bow and arrows, how have you come to this region haunted by demons?'
ramayana-3-16-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-12.translation: Thus questioned by the demoness Shurpanakha, Rama, in his straightforward way, began to tell her everything.
ramayana-3-16-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-13.translation: 'There was a king named Dasharatha, as valiant as the gods; I am his eldest son, known to people as Rama.
ramayana-3-16-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-14.translation: This is my younger brother Lakshmana, devoted to me, and this is my wife, known as Sita of Videha.
ramayana-3-16-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-15.translation: Bound by the command of my father the king and my mother, wanting dharma and for the sake of dharma, I have come to live here in the forest.
ramayana-3-16-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-16.translation: But I would like to know you. Tell me, who are you, whose are you, and why have you come here? Tell me truly.'
ramayana-3-16-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-17.translation: Hearing this, the demoness, tormented by desire, said: 'Listen, Rama, I will tell you the truth.
ramayana-3-16-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-18.translation: I am the demoness named Shurpanakha, able to take any form. I roam this forest alone, terrifying everyone.
ramayana-3-16-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-19.translation: My brother is the demon Ravana, lord of demons, and the mighty Kumbhakarna, who is always deep in sleep.
ramayana-3-16-19.meaning: Her brothers are Ravana and Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-3-16-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-20.translation: Vibhishana is righteous and does not act like a demon; and my brothers Khara and Dushana are famed for valour in battle.
ramayana-3-16-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-21.translation: I surpass them, Rama, and since first seeing you I have come to you with love as my husband, best of men. Be my husband for ever; what will you do with Sita?
ramayana-3-16-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-22.translation: She is misshapen and ugly, not fit for you. I alone am suited to you; look on me as your wife.
ramayana-3-16-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-23.translation: I will eat this ugly, unchaste, hideous, hollow-bellied human woman, together with your brother.
ramayana-3-16-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-24.translation: Then, beloved, you will roam the Dandaka with me, seeing mountain peaks and many forests.'
ramayana-3-16-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-16-25.translation: Thus addressed, Rama, skilled in speech, laughed at the woman with intoxicated eyes and began to say:
ramayana-3-16-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 16: the demoness Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, sees Rama at Panchavati and asks him to marry her.

ramayana-3-17-1.translation: Rama, smiling, spoke at his pleasure in a smooth voice to Shurpanakha, caught in the noose of desire:
ramayana-3-17-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-2.translation: 'I am married, lady; this is my beloved wife. For women like you, having a co-wife would be very painful.
ramayana-3-17-2.meaning: He told her he was married.
ramayana-3-17-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-3.translation: But this younger brother of mine is of good character, handsome, glorious, unmarried and valiant; his name is Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-17-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara. The brothers' teasing and the mutilation are hard parts of the story; many readers see them as a reminder that even heroes act harshly, and the episode sets the war in motion.

ramayana-3-17-4.translation: He is young, handsome and wants a wife, never having had one; he will be a fitting husband for your beauty.
ramayana-3-17-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-5.translation: Take my brother as your husband, large-eyed one, without a rival wife, like sunlight on Mount Meru.'
ramayana-3-17-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-6.translation: Thus addressed by Rama, the demoness, blinded by desire, abruptly left Rama and said to Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-17-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-7.translation: 'I, fair-skinned, am the wife suited to your beauty; with me you will roam all the Dandaka happily.'
ramayana-3-17-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-8.translation: Thus addressed by the demoness, Lakshmana, skilled in speech, smiled and said to Shurpanakha:
ramayana-3-17-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-9.translation: 'How can you want to be the slave-wife of a slave like me? I am dependent on my noble brother, lotus-coloured one.
ramayana-3-17-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-10.translation: Be the younger wife of my noble brother, large-eyed one, whose fortune is great; you will have your wish, joyful and fair.
ramayana-3-17-10.meaning: He sent her back to Rama.
ramayana-3-17-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-11.translation: He will leave this ugly, unchaste, hideous, hollow-bellied, old wife and turn to you alone.
ramayana-3-17-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara. The brothers' teasing and the mutilation are hard parts of the story; many readers see them as a reminder that even heroes act harshly, and the episode sets the war in motion.

ramayana-3-17-12.translation: For what wise man would give up this excellent beauty and set his heart on human women, lovely one?'
ramayana-3-17-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-13.translation: Told this by Lakshmana, the hideous, hollow-bellied demoness, not understanding jokes, took his words as true.
ramayana-3-17-13.meaning: She did not see the mockery.
ramayana-3-17-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-14.translation: Blinded by desire, she said to Rama, the unassailable subduer of foes, seated with Sita in the leaf hut:
ramayana-3-17-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-15.translation: 'Clinging to this ugly, unchaste, hideous, hollow-bellied, old wife, you do not value me.
ramayana-3-17-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-16.translation: Today, while you watch, I will eat this human woman and live happily with you without a rival.'
ramayana-3-17-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-17.translation: Saying this, her eyes like burning torches, she rushed in fury at fawn-eyed Sita, like a great meteor at the star Rohini.
ramayana-3-17-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-18.translation: As she fell upon them like the noose of death, mighty Rama, angry, held her back and said to Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-17-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-19.translation: 'One should never joke with cruel, ignoble beings, Lakshmana. Look at Sita, barely alive, gentle one.
ramayana-3-17-19.meaning: Rama admitted the joke went wrong.
ramayana-3-17-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara. Rama himself recognises that the teasing was a mistake.

ramayana-3-17-20.translation: You should disfigure this ugly, unchaste, wildly drunk, pot-bellied demoness, tiger among men.'
ramayana-3-17-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-21.translation: Thus told, angry Lakshmana drew his sword in front of Rama and cut off her ears and nose.
ramayana-3-17-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara. The brothers' teasing and the mutilation are hard parts of the story; many readers see them as a reminder that even heroes act harshly, and the episode sets the war in motion.

ramayana-3-17-22.translation: With ears and nose cut off, the terrible Shurpanakha screamed in a broken voice and ran back into the forest the way she had come.
ramayana-3-17-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-23.translation: Disfigured, terrible, drenched in blood, the demoness roared many kinds of roars, like a rain cloud in the monsoon.
ramayana-3-17-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-24.translation: Dripping blood, dreadful to see, she raised her arms and roared as she entered the great forest.
ramayana-3-17-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-25.translation: Then, disfigured, she went to Khara in Janasthana, surrounded by hosts of demons, her brother of fierce energy, and fell to the ground before him like a thunderbolt from the sky.
ramayana-3-17-25.meaning: She went to her brother Khara.
ramayana-3-17-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-17-26.translation: Then, faint with fear and confusion, bloodied, Khara's sister told him everything: that Rama had come to the forest with his wife and Lakshmana, and how she was disfigured.
ramayana-3-17-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 17: the brothers mock Shurpanakha; when she lunges at Sita, Lakshmana cuts off her ears and nose and she flees to her brother Khara.

ramayana-3-18-1.translation: Seeing his sister fallen, disfigured and bloodied, the demon Khara, burning with anger, asked:
ramayana-3-18-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-2.translation: 'You are strong and brave, go where you will and take any form; who has brought you, who are like Death, to this state?
ramayana-3-18-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-3.translation: Among gods, gandharvas, beings and great seers, who is so mighty as to have disfigured you?
ramayana-3-18-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-4.translation: For I see no one in the world who would do me harm, except the thousand-eyed great Indra, chastiser of Paka.
ramayana-3-18-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-5.translation: Today with my life-ending arrows I will take his life, as a crane drinks milk mixed with water.
ramayana-3-18-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-6.translation: Whose foaming red blood will the earth drink, when I have killed him in battle, his vital parts cut by my arrows?
ramayana-3-18-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-7.translation: Whose body will the birds gather to tear and joyfully eat the flesh of, when I have killed him in battle?
ramayana-3-18-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-8.translation: Neither gods nor gandharvas nor pishachas nor demons will be able to save that wretch once I drag him into great battle.
ramayana-3-18-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-9.translation: Recover your senses slowly and tell me who that insolent one is who overpowered you in the forest.'
ramayana-3-18-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-10.translation: Hearing her brother's words, especially as he was so angry, Shurpanakha said in tears:
ramayana-3-18-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-11.translation: 'Two young men, handsome, delicate, very strong, with large lotus eyes, wearing bark and black deerskin,
ramayana-3-18-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-12.translation: like kings of the gandharvas, bearing royal marks; whether gods or men, I cannot guess.
ramayana-3-18-12.meaning: She could not tell what they were.
ramayana-3-18-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-13.translation: And between them I saw a young woman, beautiful, slender-waisted, adorned with every ornament.
ramayana-3-18-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Khara demands to know who wounded his sister, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.

ramayana-3-18-14.translation: Because of that woman, the two of them together brought me to this state, like a helpless and wicked woman.
ramayana-3-18-14.meaning: She blamed Sita for her disfigurement.
ramayana-3-18-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-15.translation: When she, crooked in conduct, and those two are killed, I want to drink their foaming blood at the head of the battle.
ramayana-3-18-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-16.translation: This is my first wish, brother; fulfil it for me: let me drink her blood and theirs in battle.'
ramayana-3-18-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-17.translation: As she spoke, Khara in anger ordered fourteen mighty demons, like Death itself:
ramayana-3-18-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-18.translation: 'Two men, armed, wearing bark and black deerskin, have entered the dreadful Dandaka forest with a woman.
ramayana-3-18-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-19.translation: Kill the two and that wicked woman and come back; my sister will drink their blood.
ramayana-3-18-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-20.translation: This is my sister's cherished wish, demons; go quickly and crush those two with your strength.'
ramayana-3-18-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-18-21.translation: So commanded, the fourteen demons went there with her like clouds driven by the wind.
ramayana-3-18-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 18: Shurpanakha asks for revenge, and Khara sends fourteen powerful demons against Rama.

ramayana-3-19-1.translation: Then terrible Shurpanakha came to Rama's hermitage and pointed out to the demons the two brothers and Sita.
ramayana-3-19-1.meaning: She showed them where Rama was.
ramayana-3-19-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-2.translation: They saw mighty Rama sitting in the leaf hut with Sita and Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-19-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-3.translation: Seeing them and the demoness who had come, glorious Rama said to his radiant brother Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-19-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-4.translation: 'Stay close to Sita for a moment, Lakshmana. I will kill these who have followed her here.'
ramayana-3-19-4.meaning: Rama protected Sita and faced them.
ramayana-3-19-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-5.translation: Hearing these words of self-aware Rama, Lakshmana said 'So be it' and honoured them.
ramayana-3-19-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-6.translation: The righteous Rama strung his great gold-adorned bow and said to the demons:
ramayana-3-19-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-7.translation: 'We are Rama and Lakshmana, brothers, sons of Dasharatha, who have entered the hard Dandaka forest with Sita.
ramayana-3-19-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-8.translation: We live on fruits and roots, self-controlled, ascetics following dharma, living in the Dandaka forest. Why do you attack us?
ramayana-3-19-8.meaning: He asked why they came to harm.
ramayana-3-19-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-9.translation: At the request of the sages I have come with my bow to kill you wicked ones who harm them in the great forest.
ramayana-3-19-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-10.translation: Stay where you are and be content; do not come closer. If you value your lives, turn back, night-roamers.'
ramayana-3-19-10.meaning: Rama gave them a chance to leave.
ramayana-3-19-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows. Rama offers a warning before fighting.

ramayana-3-19-11.translation: Hearing his words, the fourteen brahmin-killing demons, spears in hand, spoke in great anger,
ramayana-3-19-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-12.translation: the dreadful ones with blood-red eyes, harsh in speech, to Rama, red-cornered of eye, sweet of speech, whose valour they had not seen:
ramayana-3-19-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-13.translation: 'Having roused the anger of our lord, the great Khara, you will lose your life today, killed by us in battle.
ramayana-3-19-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-14.translation: What power have you, one man against many at the head of battle, even to stand before us, let alone fight?
ramayana-3-19-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-15.translation: Struck by the clubs, spears and axes flung from our arms, you will lose your life, your strength and the bow gripped in your hand.'
ramayana-3-19-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-16.translation: Saying this, the fourteen furious demons rushed at Rama, swords and weapons raised, and hurled their spears at the invincible Rama.
ramayana-3-19-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-17.translation: Rama cut all fourteen spears apart with as many gold-adorned arrows.
ramayana-3-19-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-18.translation: Then the mighty one, enraged, took up fourteen iron arrows, sharpened on stone, bright as the sun.
ramayana-3-19-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-19.translation: Taking them, drawing his bow and aiming at the demons, Rama released the arrows like Indra hurling thunderbolts.
ramayana-3-19-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-20.translation: The gold-feathered, blazing arrows, adorned with gold, were as bright in the sky as great meteors.
ramayana-3-19-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-21.translation: Piercing the demons' chests with force, bathed in blood, they fell to earth and sank into it with a sound like thunder.
ramayana-3-19-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-22.translation: Their hearts pierced, they fell to the ground like trees cut at the root, their bodies wet with blood, disfigured and lifeless.
ramayana-3-19-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-23.translation: Seeing them fallen, the demoness, faint with anger and terrified, let out a dreadful cry again.
ramayana-3-19-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-24.translation: Roaring loudly, Shurpanakha rushed back to Khara, her blood partly dried, and fell down again in distress, like a creeper oozing sap.
ramayana-3-19-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-19-25.translation: Having seen the demons felled in battle, Shurpanakha ran and told Khara, her brother, all about their slaughter.
ramayana-3-19-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 19: Rama warns the fourteen demons to turn back, then kills them all with fourteen arrows.

ramayana-3-20-1.translation: Seeing Shurpanakha fallen again, Khara in anger spoke clearly to her, who had come for disaster:
ramayana-3-20-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-2.translation: 'I have just sent those brave, blood-drinking demons to do what you want; why are you crying again?
ramayana-3-20-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-3.translation: They are devoted, loyal and always good to me; they cannot be killed even when struck, and would never fail to obey me.
ramayana-3-20-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-4.translation: What is this? I want to hear why you writhe on the ground like a snake, crying "O protector!"
ramayana-3-20-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-5.translation: Why do you lament as if helpless when I, your protector, am here? Get up, get up, do not fear; give up this distress.'
ramayana-3-20-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-6.translation: Thus addressed and comforted by Khara, the unassailable one wiped her tearful eyes and said to her brother:
ramayana-3-20-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-7.translation: 'You sent those fourteen brave, fearsome demons to kill Rama and Lakshmana for my sake.
ramayana-3-20-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-8.translation: But, furious, with spears and axes in hand, they were all killed in battle by Rama with arrows that pierce the vitals.
ramayana-3-20-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-9.translation: Seeing those mighty ones fall to the ground in an instant, and Rama's great feat, great terror came over me.
ramayana-3-20-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-10.translation: Frightened, alarmed and despondent, seeing danger everywhere, I have come to you again for refuge, night-roamer.
ramayana-3-20-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-11.translation: Why do you not save me, drowning in a vast ocean of grief infested with the crocodiles of despair and garlanded with waves of terror?
ramayana-3-20-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-12.translation: These flesh-eating demons who followed me have been killed on the ground by Rama's sharp arrows.
ramayana-3-20-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-13.translation: If you have any pity for me and for those demons, if you have the power and spirit to face Rama, kill that thorn in the side of the demons who live in the Dandaka forest.
ramayana-3-20-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-14.translation: If you do not kill Rama, my enemy, today, I will shamelessly give up my life right in front of you.
ramayana-3-20-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-15.translation: I see clearly that you cannot stand face to face with Rama in battle when he holds his bow.
ramayana-3-20-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-16.translation: You think yourself a hero but you are not; your valour is falsely claimed, since you cannot kill two men, Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-20-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

keywords.meaning: one who thinks himself a hero

ramayana-3-20-17.translation: Leave Janasthana quickly with your kin. What place is there here for one without courage and of little strength?
ramayana-3-20-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-20-18.translation: Overpowered by Rama's might, you will soon perish. For Rama, son of Dasharatha, is full of power, and so is his very valiant brother, who disfigured me.'
ramayana-3-20-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 20: Shurpanakha returns to Khara in despair and taunts him into fighting Rama himself.

ramayana-3-21-1.translation: Thus provoked by Shurpanakha, brave Khara spoke still harsher words among the demons:
ramayana-3-21-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-2.translation: 'This boundless anger of mine, born of your humiliation, cannot be held back, like the rising salt sea.
ramayana-3-21-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-3.translation: I do not count Rama, a mere man whose life is spent, as valiant; by his own misdeeds he will lose his life today.
ramayana-3-21-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-4.translation: Stop these tears and give up this panic; I will send Rama and his brother to Yama's abode.
ramayana-3-21-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-5.translation: Today, demoness, you will drink the hot red blood of Rama, struck down by my axe and dying on the ground.'
ramayana-3-21-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-6.translation: Delighted at the words from Khara's mouth, she foolishly praised her brother, the best of demons, once more.
ramayana-3-21-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-7.translation: First insulted by her, then praised, Khara said to his general named Dushana:
ramayana-3-21-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-8.translation: 'Fourteen thousand demons who follow my will, of terrible speed, who never retreat in battle,
ramayana-3-21-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-9.translation: dark as blue clouds, dreadful, cruel in deeds, roaming the world like lions, strong and fierce,
ramayana-3-21-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-10.translation: proud as tigers, huge-mouthed and powerful, eager for battle; get them all ready, gentle one.
ramayana-3-21-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-11.translation: Bring my chariot quickly, gentle one, and bows, arrows of many colours, swords and many kinds of sharp spears.
ramayana-3-21-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-12.translation: I, skilled in war, wish to go out in front of the great descendants of Pulastya to kill the insolent Rama.'
ramayana-3-21-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-13.translation: As he spoke, Dushana reported that the great sun-coloured chariot was ready, yoked to fine dappled horses.
ramayana-3-21-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-14.translation: It was like a peak of Meru, adorned with refined gold, with golden wheels, roomy, its pole of beryl,
ramayana-3-21-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-15.translation: covered with golden fish, flowers, trees, mountains, moons and suns, auspicious flocks of birds and stars,
ramayana-3-21-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-16.translation: fitted with banners and swords, adorned with little bells and yoked to fine horses; Khara mounted it in his rage.
ramayana-3-21-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-17.translation: Seeing him in his chariot, the demons of terrible valour stood around him and mighty Dushana.
ramayana-3-21-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-18.translation: Seeing all the demons, great archers with dreadful shields, weapons and banners, Khara in his chariot said, 'March!'
ramayana-3-21-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-19.translation: Then that demon army, with dreadful shields, weapons and banners, went out of Janasthana with a great roar and great speed.
ramayana-3-21-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-20.translation: with hammers, axes, spears, sharp hatchets, swords, discuses and gleaming javelins in hand,
ramayana-3-21-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-21.translation: with lances, dreadful clubs, huge bows, maces, swords, pestles and thunderbolts, terrible to see,
ramayana-3-21-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-22.translation: fourteen thousand very dreadful demons who followed Khara's will marched out of Janasthana.
ramayana-3-21-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-23.translation: Seeing the demons of terrible valour rushing forward, Khara's chariot went a little after them.
ramayana-3-21-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-24.translation: Then, knowing Khara's wish, the charioteer urged on the dappled horses adorned with refined gold.
ramayana-3-21-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-25.translation: Driven fast, the chariot of Khara, killer of foes, filled every direction with its sound.
ramayana-3-21-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-21-26.translation: Khara, his fury growing, harsh-voiced, hurrying like Death to kill his enemy, roared and urged on his charioteer again, like a mighty cloud raining stones.
ramayana-3-21-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 21: Khara orders his army of fourteen thousand demons, mounts his chariot and marches out of Janasthana.

ramayana-3-22-1.translation: As that dreadful army set out, a huge, roaring, donkey-grey cloud rained down inauspicious, blood-coloured water.
ramayana-3-22-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-2.translation: His very swift horses, yoked to the chariot, fell by chance on a level, flower-strewn royal road.
ramayana-3-22-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-3.translation: A dark halo edged with blood, like a wheel of fire, encircled the sun.
ramayana-3-22-3.meaning: The sun had an ominous halo.
ramayana-3-22-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-4.translation: Then a huge, very dreadful vulture came and perched on the tall gold-staffed banner.
ramayana-3-22-4.meaning: A vulture sat on his flag.
ramayana-3-22-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-5.translation: Near Janasthana, flesh-eating beasts and birds with harsh voices gathered and made many discordant sounds.
ramayana-3-22-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-6.translation: Inauspicious jackals, ill-omened for those who set out, howled terribly with great cries toward the blazing quarter.
ramayana-3-22-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-7.translation: Dreadful clouds like broken mountains, carrying blood for water, made the sky no sky.
ramayana-3-22-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-8.translation: A dreadful, hair-raising darkness arose; neither the main nor the intermediate directions could be clearly seen.
ramayana-3-22-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-9.translation: The sky shone the colour of fresh blood though it was not twilight; dreadful beasts and birds cried out facing Khara.
ramayana-3-22-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-10.translation: Jackals, always bringing ill in battle, dreadful to see, howled facing the army with flame-spitting mouths.
ramayana-3-22-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-11.translation: A headless trunk like an iron bar was seen near the sun, and the great planet Rahu seized the sun out of season.
ramayana-3-22-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-12.translation: The wind blew fiercely, the sun lost its light, and stars bright as fireflies rose though it was not night.
ramayana-3-22-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-13.translation: At that moment, the lotus ponds, their fish and birds hidden, lost their flowers, and the trees were left without flowers or fruit.
ramayana-3-22-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride.

ramayana-3-22-14.translation: Dust as red as clouds rose without wind, and myna birds cried 'vichi kuchi' there.
ramayana-3-22-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-15.translation: Meteors fell with a roar, dreadful to see, and the earth shook with its mountains and forests.
ramayana-3-22-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-16.translation: As wise Khara roared in his chariot, his left arm trembled and his voice faltered.
ramayana-3-22-16.meaning: Bad signs in his own body.
ramayana-3-22-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-17.translation: His eyes filled with tears as he looked about, and pain arose in his forehead; yet in his delusion he did not turn back.
ramayana-3-22-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama. Pride blinds Khara to every warning.

ramayana-3-22-18.translation: Seeing these great, hair-raising portents arise, Khara laughed and said to all the demons:
ramayana-3-22-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-19.translation: 'I do not care about all these dreadful portents, by my strength, as a strong man does not care about the weak.
ramayana-3-22-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-20.translation: I could bring down even the stars from the sky with sharp arrows; in my anger I could make Death himself die.
ramayana-3-22-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-21.translation: I will not return without killing Rama, proud of his strength, and his brother Lakshmana with sharp arrows.
ramayana-3-22-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-22.translation: Let my sister have her wish and drink their blood, she for whose sake this reversal has come to Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-22-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-23.translation: I have never before met defeat in battle; you have seen this yourselves, I do not lie.
ramayana-3-22-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-24.translation: In my anger I could kill even the king of gods riding his rutting Airavata, thunderbolt in hand; how much more two men.'
ramayana-3-22-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-25.translation: Hearing the demon's roar, the great army, bound in the noose of death, felt boundless joy.
ramayana-3-22-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-26.translation: Great souls gathered, eager to watch the battle: sages, gods, gandharvas, perfected beings and celestial singers.
ramayana-3-22-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-27.translation: Gathered together, those of holy deeds said to one another: 'May there be welfare for cows and brahmins and those honoured in the worlds.
ramayana-3-22-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-28.translation: May Rama defeat the night-roaming descendants of Pulastya in battle, as the discus-holder Vishnu defeated all the chief asuras.'
ramayana-3-22-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-29.translation: Saying this and much else, the great seers watched the army of those demons whose lives were spent.
ramayana-3-22-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-30.translation: Khara rushed out ahead of the army in his chariot; seeing him, the demons rushed out again too.
ramayana-3-22-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-31.translation: Shyenagamin, Prithugriva, Yajnashatru, Vihangama, Durjaya, Karaviraksha, Parusha, Kalakarmuka,
ramayana-3-22-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-32.translation: Meghamali, Mahamali, Sarpasya and Rudhirashana: these twelve mighty ones went on around Khara.
ramayana-3-22-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-33.translation: Mahakapala, Sthulaksha, Pramathin and Trishiras, these four army leaders, followed behind Dushana.
ramayana-3-22-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-22-34.translation: That dreadful army of demon heroes, of terrible speed and eager for battle, suddenly fell upon the two princes, like planets upon the moon and sun.
ramayana-3-22-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 22: terrible omens appear as Khara's army advances, but Khara ignores them in his pride, while sages gather to watch and bless Rama.

ramayana-3-23-1.translation: As Khara of fierce valour went toward the hermitage, Rama with his brother saw those same portents.
ramayana-3-23-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-2.translation: Seeing those very dreadful, hair-raising portents, harmful to creatures, he said to Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-23-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-3.translation: 'See, mighty-armed one, these great portents that destroy all beings have arisen to destroy all the demons.
ramayana-3-23-3.meaning: The omens point to the demons' end.
ramayana-3-23-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-4.translation: These harsh, donkey-grey clouds move about the sky, pouring streams of blood with harsh sounds.
ramayana-3-23-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-5.translation: All my arrows, eager for battle, are smoking, and my gold-backed bows are quivering, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-23-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-6.translation: From the way the forest birds are crying, danger lies ahead of us and our lives are at stake.
ramayana-3-23-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-7.translation: There will be a very great battle, no doubt; my arm, throbbing again and again, tells me so.
ramayana-3-23-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-8.translation: But close at hand, hero, victory for us and defeat for the enemy are shown, for your face looks bright and clear.
ramayana-3-23-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-9.translation: For those ready for battle whose face is dull, Lakshmana, life is coming to its end.
ramayana-3-23-9.meaning: A dull face is a sign of doom.
ramayana-3-23-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-10.translation: A wise man who wants good and suspects danger should make provision for what has not yet come.
ramayana-3-23-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army. A practical teaching on foresight.

ramayana-3-23-11.translation: So take Sita and, with bow and arrows in hand, go to the cave in the mountain, hard to reach and thick with trees.
ramayana-3-23-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-12.translation: I do not want you to oppose these words. I bind you by my feet: go quickly, child.'
ramayana-3-23-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-13.translation: Thus told by Rama, Lakshmana took his bow and arrows and went with Sita to the hard-to-reach cave.
ramayana-3-23-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-14.translation: When Lakshmana had entered the cave with Sita, Rama said, 'Good, it is done,' and put on his armour.
ramayana-3-23-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-15.translation: Adorned with that fire-bright armour, Rama looked like a smokeless fire risen in darkness.
ramayana-3-23-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-16.translation: Raising his great bow and taking his arrows, the valiant one stood there, filling the directions with the twang of his bowstring.
ramayana-3-23-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-17.translation: Then the gods, gandharvas, perfected beings, celestial singers and guhyakas, greatly alarmed, said to one another:
ramayana-3-23-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-18.translation: 'Fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds, and the righteous Rama alone; how will this battle go?'
ramayana-3-23-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-19.translation: Then the army of demons, with deep roars and dreadful armour, weapons and banners, appeared on every side.
ramayana-3-23-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-20.translation: They roared like lions, bellowed at one another, twanged their bows and yawned again and again.
ramayana-3-23-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-21.translation: The tumultuous sound of their shouting and beating of drums filled that forest.
ramayana-3-23-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-22.translation: Frightened by that sound, the wild animals of the forest fled to where it was silent and did not look back.
ramayana-3-23-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-23.translation: That army, of great speed, armed with many weapons, deep as the ocean, approached Rama.
ramayana-3-23-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-24.translation: Rama too, skilled in battle, looking everywhere, saw Khara's army ready for battle.
ramayana-3-23-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-25.translation: Drawing his dreadful bow and taking arrows from his quiver, he summoned fierce anger to kill all the demons.
ramayana-3-23-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-23-26.translation: Enraged, blazing like the fire at the end of an age, he became hard to look at; seeing him filled with power, the forest deities trembled.
ramayana-3-23-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

keywords.meaning: fire at the end of an age

ramayana-3-23-27.translation: The form of angry Rama then looked like that of Shiva, bearer of Pinaka, ready to destroy Daksha's sacrifice.
ramayana-3-23-27.meaning: He looked like Shiva in wrath.
ramayana-3-23-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama reads the omens, sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave for safety, puts on armour and waits alone for the army.

ramayana-3-24-1.translation: Arriving at the hermitage with his vanguard, Khara saw Rama, angry, killer of foes, gripping his bow.
ramayana-3-24-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-2.translation: Seeing him, Khara raised his strung bow with its harsh twang and told his charioteer, 'Drive toward Rama.'
ramayana-3-24-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-3.translation: At Khara's command the charioteer urged the horses toward where mighty-armed Rama stood alone, shaking his bow.
ramayana-3-24-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-4.translation: Seeing him rush out, all the night-roamers, his ministers, surrounded him with great roars.
ramayana-3-24-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-5.translation: Khara, in his chariot among those demons, looked like Mars risen among the stars.
ramayana-3-24-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-6.translation: Then all the angry night-roamers showered the invincible Rama, of terrible bow, with many kinds of weapons.
ramayana-3-24-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-7.translation: With iron hammers, spears, lances, swords and axes, the furious demons struck at Rama in battle.
ramayana-3-24-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-8.translation: Those huge, loud, mighty ones, like clouds, rushed at Rama in battle, eager to kill him.
ramayana-3-24-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-9.translation: Those hordes of demons rained showers of arrows on Rama, as great clouds pour streams on the king of mountains.
ramayana-3-24-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-10.translation: Surrounded by those dreadful hosts of demons, Rama was like Mahadeva surrounded by his attendants on holy days.
ramayana-3-24-10.meaning: He stood among them like Shiva.
ramayana-3-24-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-11.translation: Rama received the weapons the demons released with his arrows, as the ocean receives the floods of rivers.
ramayana-3-24-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-12.translation: Though his body was wounded by those dreadful weapons, Rama did not waver, like a great mountain struck by many blazing thunderbolts.
ramayana-3-24-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-13.translation: Pierced and smeared with blood all over his body, Rama looked like the sun covered by evening clouds.
ramayana-3-24-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-14.translation: Gods, gandharvas, perfected beings and great seers grieved, seeing him alone surrounded by many thousands.
ramayana-3-24-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-15.translation: Then Rama, enraged, bent his bow into a circle and released sharp arrows by the hundred and thousand.
ramayana-3-24-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-16.translation: Hard to ward off, hard to bear, like the nooses of Death in battle, the heron-feathered, straight-flying arrows Rama released with ease.
ramayana-3-24-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-17.translation: Released by Rama with ease into the enemy army, those arrows took the demons' lives like nooses made by Time.
ramayana-3-24-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-18.translation: Piercing the demons' bodies, bathed in blood, those arrows shone in the sky with the brilliance of blazing fire.
ramayana-3-24-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-19.translation: Countless, very fierce arrows that took the demons' lives flew from the circle of Rama's bow.
ramayana-3-24-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-20.translation: With them he cut bows, banner tops, armour and heads, many arms with their ornaments, and thighs like elephants' trunks.
ramayana-3-24-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-21.translation: Then, pierced by tubular arrows, iron arrows, sharp-pointed and barbed arrows, the night-roamers let out terrible cries of pain.
ramayana-3-24-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-22.translation: That army, struck by Rama's sharp, vital-piercing arrows, found no relief, like a dry forest in a fire.
ramayana-3-24-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-23.translation: Some brave night-roamers of terrible strength, in great anger, hurled spears, swords and axes at Rama.
ramayana-3-24-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-24.translation: Warding off those weapons with arrows, mighty-armed Rama took their lives in battle and cut off their heads.
ramayana-3-24-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-25.translation: Those night-roamers who were left, despondent and wounded by arrows, ran to Khara for refuge.
ramayana-3-24-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-26.translation: Gathering them all again and encouraging them, Dushana rushed at Rama in anger, like Death at Rudra.
ramayana-3-24-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-27.translation: Turning back, all of them, fearless with Dushana's support, rushed at Rama again, armed with sala trees, palms and rocks.
ramayana-3-24-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-24-28.translation: Then there was a wondrous, tumultuous, hair-raising and very dreadful battle between Rama and those demons.
ramayana-3-24-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 24: Khara's army attacks; Rama, wounded but unshaken, cuts down the demons with a storm of arrows.

ramayana-3-25-1.translation: The righteous Rama received that great, deadly shower of trees and rocks with his sharp arrows.
ramayana-3-25-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-2.translation: Receiving that shower like a bull with eyes closed, Rama summoned the greatest anger to kill all the demons.
ramayana-3-25-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-3.translation: Then, filled with anger and blazing as if with power, he covered the army and Dushana on every side with arrows.
ramayana-3-25-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-4.translation: Then the general Dushana, destroyer of foes, in anger seized a hair-raising iron club like a mountain peak,
ramayana-3-25-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-5.translation: bound with gold bands, crusher of the armies of the gods, studded with sharp iron spikes and smeared with the fat of enemies,
ramayana-3-25-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-6.translation: as hard as a thunderbolt, able to break the gates of enemy cities, like a great serpent; seizing that club, the cruel night-roamer Dushana fell upon Rama.
ramayana-3-25-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-7.translation: As Dushana fell upon him, Rama cut off both his arms, with their ornaments, with two arrows.
ramayana-3-25-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-8.translation: His huge club fell from his severed hands at the front of the battle, like Indra's banner.
ramayana-3-25-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-9.translation: With his arms cut away, Dushana fell to the ground, like a proud great elephant whose tusks are broken.
ramayana-3-25-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-10.translation: Seeing Dushana fallen and slain in battle, all beings honoured Rama, crying 'Well done, well done!'
ramayana-3-25-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-11.translation: Meanwhile three angry army leaders, bound by the noose of death, rushed at Rama together: Mahakapala, Sthulaksha and mighty Pramathin.
ramayana-3-25-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-12.translation: The demon Mahakapala raised a huge spear, Sthulaksha seized a battle axe, and Pramathin an axe.
ramayana-3-25-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-13.translation: Seeing them rush at him, Rama received them with sharp-pointed arrows as if receiving guests who had arrived.
ramayana-3-25-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.
