ramayana-3-25-14.translation: Rama cut off Mahakapala's head and crushed Pramathin with countless floods of arrows.
ramayana-3-25-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and other demon commanders.

ramayana-3-25-15.translation: He filled Sthulaksha's eyes with sharp arrows; slain, he fell to the ground like a great tree with its branches.
ramayana-3-25-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-16.translation: Then the radiant one, with fire-bright arrows adorned with gold and diamonds, attacked what was left of the army.
ramayana-3-25-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-17.translation: Those gold-feathered arrows, like smoking fires, killed the demons as thunderbolts strike great trees.
ramayana-3-25-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-18.translation: At the head of the battle Rama killed a hundred demons with a hundred barbed arrows, and a thousand with a thousand.
ramayana-3-25-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-19.translation: Their armour and ornaments broken, their bows cut and shattered, the night-roamers fell to the ground smeared with blood.
ramayana-3-25-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-20.translation: The whole earth was strewn with them, fallen in battle with loosened hair and bathed in blood, like a great altar strewn with kusha grass.
ramayana-3-25-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-21.translation: In a moment the very dreadful forest, full of slain demons, looked like hell, a mire of flesh and blood.
ramayana-3-25-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-22.translation: Fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds were killed by Rama alone, a man on foot.
ramayana-3-25-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand. A famous feat, showing that strength rooted in right purpose prevails.

ramayana-3-25-23.translation: Of that whole army only the great warrior Khara and the demon Trishiras were left, facing Rama, slayer of foes.
ramayana-3-25-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-25-24.translation: Seeing that army of terrible strength killed in the great battle by the mightier Rama, Khara drove at him in his great chariot, like Indra with thunderbolt raised.
ramayana-3-25-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama kills the general Dushana and the other demon commanders, and alone destroys the fourteen thousand.

ramayana-3-26-1.translation: As Khara went toward Rama, the army commander, the demon named Trishiras, came up and said:
ramayana-3-26-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-2.translation: 'Send me, valiant one, and turn back from this rashness. See mighty-armed Rama brought down in battle.
ramayana-3-26-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-3.translation: I promise you truly, and touch my weapon in oath, that I will kill Rama, who deserves death from all demons.
ramayana-3-26-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-4.translation: Either I will be his death in battle or he mine. Hold back your eagerness for a moment and be a witness.
ramayana-3-26-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-5.translation: Either you will go joyfully to Janasthana when Rama is dead, or, if I am killed, you will go to fight Rama.'
ramayana-3-26-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-6.translation: Persuaded by Trishiras out of desire for death, Khara gave him leave: 'Go and fight.' He went toward Rama.
ramayana-3-26-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-7.translation: Trishiras, in his shining chariot drawn by horses, rushed at Rama in battle like a three-peaked mountain.
ramayana-3-26-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-8.translation: Releasing streams of arrows like a great cloud, he let out a roar like a drum wet with water.
ramayana-3-26-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-9.translation: Seeing the demon Trishiras coming, Rama received him with his bow, shaking sharp arrows.
ramayana-3-26-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-10.translation: That tumultuous battle between Rama and Trishiras, both very strong, was like one between a lion and an elephant.
ramayana-3-26-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-11.translation: Then, struck on the forehead by Trishiras with three arrows, Rama, angry and impatient, said fiercely:
ramayana-3-26-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-12.translation: 'Oh, such is the strength of this demon hero, by whose arrows I am wounded on the forehead as if by flowers! Now receive my arrows released from the bowstring.'
ramayana-3-26-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-13.translation: Saying this, he angrily struck Trishiras in the chest with fourteen arrows like venomous snakes.
ramayana-3-26-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-14.translation: With four smooth-jointed arrows the radiant one brought down his four horses.
ramayana-3-26-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-15.translation: With eight arrows he brought down the charioteer in the chariot, and with one arrow Rama cut down his tall banner.
ramayana-3-26-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-16.translation: As the night-roamer leapt from his ruined chariot, Rama pierced him in the heart with arrows and he went numb.
ramayana-3-26-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-17.translation: Then, with three swift arrows, Rama of boundless spirit, angry, brought down the demon's three heads.
ramayana-3-26-17.meaning: Rama cut off his three heads.
ramayana-3-26-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-18.translation: Spitting blood, crushed by Rama's arrows, the night-roamer fell to the ground after his own fallen heads.
ramayana-3-26-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-19.translation: Then the remaining demons who depended on Khara broke and ran, not standing their ground, like deer frightened by a tiger.
ramayana-3-26-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-26-20.translation: Seeing them run, Khara, enraged, turned them back himself and rushed at Rama, as Rahu at the moon.
ramayana-3-26-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 26: the three-headed demon Trishiras fights Rama and is killed.

ramayana-3-27-1.translation: Seeing Dushana and Trishiras slain in battle, and seeing Rama's valour, even Khara felt fear.
ramayana-3-27-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-2.translation: He saw the mighty, irresistible demon army, and Dushana and Trishiras too, killed by Rama alone.
ramayana-3-27-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-3.translation: Seeing that army mostly destroyed, the demon Khara, dejected, approached Rama as Namuchi approached Indra.
ramayana-3-27-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-4.translation: Drawing his strong bow, Khara shot blood-drinking iron arrows at Rama like angry venomous snakes.
ramayana-3-27-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-5.translation: Twanging his bowstring again and again and showing his skill in weapons, Khara moved about the battlefield in his chariot, shooting arrows.
ramayana-3-27-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-6.translation: The great warrior filled all the directions and intermediate directions with arrows; seeing this, Rama too took up his great bow.
ramayana-3-27-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-7.translation: With unbearable arrows like sparking fires, he left no gap in the sky, like the rain god with his showers.
ramayana-3-27-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-8.translation: With sharp arrows released by Khara and Rama, the whole sky became no sky, filled with arrows on every side.
ramayana-3-27-8.meaning: The sky was full of arrows.
ramayana-3-27-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-9.translation: Covered by a net of arrows, the sun did not shine, as the two fought, each eager to kill the other.
ramayana-3-27-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-10.translation: Then he struck Rama in battle with tubular, iron, sharp-pointed and barbed arrows, like goads on a great elephant.
ramayana-3-27-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-11.translation: All beings saw the demon standing in his chariot, bow in hand, like Death with a noose in his hand.
ramayana-3-27-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-12.translation: Seeing him, valiant as a lion and moving like a lion, Rama was not alarmed, as a lion is not alarmed by a small deer.
ramayana-3-27-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-13.translation: Then Khara in his great sun-bright chariot came at Rama in battle, like a moth to fire.
ramayana-3-27-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-14.translation: Then Khara, showing his speed of hand, cut great Rama's bow, with its arrow, at the grip.
ramayana-3-27-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-15.translation: Then, angry, he took seven more arrows bright as Indra's thunderbolt and struck Rama's armour in battle.
ramayana-3-27-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-16.translation: Struck by Khara's well-jointed arrows, the armour of sun-bright Rama fell to the ground.
ramayana-3-27-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-17.translation: Pierced by arrows all over his body, angry Rama shone in battle like a smokeless blazing fire.
ramayana-3-27-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-18.translation: Then Rama, destroyer of enemies, strung another great bow with a deep roar, to put an end to his foe.
ramayana-3-27-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-19.translation: Raising that excellent, very great bow of Vishnu, given to him by the great seer, he rushed at Khara.
ramayana-3-27-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-20.translation: Then, enraged, Rama cut down Khara's banner in battle with gold-feathered, smooth-jointed arrows.
ramayana-3-27-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-21.translation: That handsome golden banner, cut into many pieces, fell to the earth like the sun at the gods' command.
ramayana-3-27-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-22.translation: Angry Khara, who knew the vital points, struck Rama in the body and heart with four arrows, as one strikes an elephant with javelins.
ramayana-3-27-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-23.translation: Pierced by many arrows from Khara's bow, his limbs drenched with blood, Rama became very angry.
ramayana-3-27-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-24.translation: The best of bowmen, the great archer, took his bow in that great battle and shot six well-aimed arrows.
ramayana-3-27-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-25.translation: He struck him with one arrow in the head, two in the arms, and three crescent-headed ones in the chest.
ramayana-3-27-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-26.translation: Then the mighty one, angry and eager to kill the demon, took thirteen sun-bright iron arrows sharpened on stone.
ramayana-3-27-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-27.translation: With one he broke the yoke, with four the four horses, and with the sixth he cut off the head of Khara's charioteer in battle.
ramayana-3-27-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-28.translation: With three the mighty one broke the triple bamboo pole, with two the axle; with the twelfth arrow Rama, as if laughing, cut Khara's bow and arrow, and with the thirteenth, like a thunderbolt, Indra-like Rama pierced Khara in battle.
ramayana-3-27-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-29.translation: With his bow broken, chariotless, his horses and charioteer killed, Khara leapt down and stood on the ground, mace in hand.
ramayana-3-27-29.meaning: Khara stood on foot with a mace.
ramayana-3-27-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-27-30.translation: Gathered together, the gods and great seers, standing in their celestial chariots, joyfully honoured that feat of the great warrior Rama with joined palms.
ramayana-3-27-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 27: Khara himself fights Rama, breaks his bow and armour, but Rama takes up Vishnu's bow and destroys Khara's chariot.

ramayana-3-28-1.translation: To Khara, standing chariotless with mace in hand, mighty Rama spoke harsh words, gently at first:
ramayana-3-28-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-2.translation: 'Standing in your great army crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, you have done very cruel deeds, hated by all the world.
ramayana-3-28-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-3.translation: One who frightens beings, who is cruel and does evil deeds, does not last, even if he is lord of the three worlds.
ramayana-3-28-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters. A key moral teaching.

ramayana-3-28-4.translation: Everyone kills one who does deeds against the world, night-roamer, as they kill a vicious snake that comes near.
ramayana-3-28-4.meaning: The cruel are destroyed by all.
ramayana-3-28-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-5.translation: He who does evil out of greed or desire without realising it sees his end when he falls, like the brahmani lizard from hail.
ramayana-3-28-5.meaning: Greed blinds one to the coming fall.
ramayana-3-28-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-6.translation: What fruit will you gain, demon, by killing the noble ascetics who follow dharma living in the Dandaka forest?
ramayana-3-28-6.meaning: What good comes from killing the innocent?
ramayana-3-28-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-7.translation: Cruel doers of evil, hated by the world, do not last long even when they gain power, like trees with rotten roots.
ramayana-3-28-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-8.translation: The doer surely reaps the dreadful fruit of his evil deed when the time comes, as a tree bears its seasonal flower.
ramayana-3-28-8.meaning: Every deed bears its fruit in time.
ramayana-3-28-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters. A clear statement of the law of karma.

ramayana-3-28-9.translation: Before long in this world the fruit of evil deeds is reaped, night-roamer, as with poisoned food that has been eaten.
ramayana-3-28-9.meaning: Evil soon returns to its doer.
ramayana-3-28-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-10.translation: I, a king, have come to take the lives of those who do dreadful evil and wish harm on the world, night-roamer.
ramayana-3-28-10.meaning: Rama's duty is to stop evil.
ramayana-3-28-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-11.translation: Today my gold-adorned arrows will tear through you and fall, as snakes into an anthill.
ramayana-3-28-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-12.translation: Today, killed in battle with your army, you will follow those followers of dharma whom you devoured in the Dandaka forest.
ramayana-3-28-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-13.translation: Today let the great seers whom you harmed before, standing in their celestial chariots, see you killed by arrows and in hell.
ramayana-3-28-13.meaning: The sages will see justice done.
ramayana-3-28-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-14.translation: Strike as you please, make your effort, lowest of your clan; today I will bring down your head like a palm fruit.'
ramayana-3-28-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-15.translation: Thus addressed by Rama, Khara, angry, his eyes red, laughed and answered Rama, faint with anger:
ramayana-3-28-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-16.translation: 'Having killed ordinary demons in battle, son of Dasharatha, how can you praise yourself, who deserve no praise?
ramayana-3-28-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-17.translation: Truly valiant and strong men, bulls among men, say nothing, proud in their own power.
ramayana-3-28-17.meaning: The truly brave do not boast.
ramayana-3-28-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-18.translation: It is common, undisciplined men, disgraces to the warrior class, who boast pointlessly, Rama, as you do.
ramayana-3-28-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-19.translation: What hero in battle, naming his family, praises himself unprompted when the time of death has come?
ramayana-3-28-19.meaning: Who boasts at the hour of death?
ramayana-3-28-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-20.translation: Your boasting has shown your lightness completely, like a kusha fire made to look like gold.
ramayana-3-28-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-21.translation: Do you not see me standing here with my mace, unshakeable like a mountain studded with minerals?
ramayana-3-28-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-22.translation: With mace in hand I am enough to take your life in battle, like Death with noose in hand for the three worlds.
ramayana-3-28-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-23.translation: Much could be said to you, but I will not say it; the sun may set and then there would be a break in the fight.
ramayana-3-28-23.meaning: He wanted to fight, not talk.
ramayana-3-28-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-24.translation: You have killed fourteen thousand demons; by your death today I will wipe away their tears.'
ramayana-3-28-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-25.translation: Saying this, in great anger Khara hurled at Rama that mace with its fine bands, blazing like lightning.
ramayana-3-28-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-26.translation: Released from Khara's arm, that huge blazing mace reduced trees and shrubs to ashes as it came near.
ramayana-3-28-26.meaning: The mace burned all in its path.
ramayana-3-28-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-27.translation: As that blazing mace, like the noose of death, came through the air, Rama cut it into many pieces with arrows.
ramayana-3-28-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-28-28.translation: Broken and shattered by arrows, it fell to the ground like a she-serpent brought down by spells and herbs.
ramayana-3-28-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 28: Rama tells Khara that wrongdoing always bears fruit; Khara boasts and hurls his mace, which Rama shatters.

ramayana-3-29-1.translation: Having broken the mace with arrows, Rama, lover of dharma, smiling, spoke these angry words to Khara:
ramayana-3-29-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama answers Khara's boasts before the final duel.

ramayana-3-29-2.translation: 'You have shown the whole of your strength, lowest of demons; you are weaker than I, and your roaring was in vain.
ramayana-3-29-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama answers Khara's boasts before the final duel.

ramayana-3-29-3.translation: This mace, shattered by my arrows and fallen to the ground, has destroyed the confidence of you who are bold only in words.
ramayana-3-29-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-4.translation: What you said, that you would wipe away the tears of the slain demons, that too is a false statement.
ramayana-3-29-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-5.translation: I will take the life of this low, mean-natured, false demon, as Garuda took the nectar of immortality.
ramayana-3-29-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-6.translation: Today the earth will drink your blood, adorned with froth and bubbles, when your throat is split and you are torn by my arrows.
ramayana-3-29-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-7.translation: With every limb covered in dust and both arms flung out, you will sleep embracing the earth like a rare woman.
ramayana-3-29-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-8.translation: When you, disgrace of the demons, lie in your long sleep, this Dandaka forest will be a refuge for those without refuge.
ramayana-3-29-8.meaning: His death will make the forest safe.
ramayana-3-29-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-9.translation: When Janasthana, your stronghold, is destroyed by my arrows, the sages will roam the forest everywhere without fear.
ramayana-3-29-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-10.translation: Today the demonesses, who brought fear to others, will flee in fear, their kin slain, their faces wet with tears, wretched.
ramayana-3-29-10.meaning: Fear returns to those who caused it.
ramayana-3-29-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-11.translation: Today your wives, of fitting family, whose husband is such as you, will know the taste of grief, night-roamer.
ramayana-3-29-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-12.translation: Cruel-natured, mean-souled, ever a thorn to brahmins, because of you the sages pour their offerings into the fire in fear.'
ramayana-3-29-12.meaning: Khara made worship a fearful thing.
ramayana-3-29-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-13.translation: As Rama spoke so angrily in battle, Khara, in fury, scolded him in an even harsher voice:
ramayana-3-29-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-14.translation: 'You are truly very arrogant, and fearless even amid danger; in the power of death, you do not know what should and should not be said.
ramayana-3-29-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-15.translation: For men caught in the noose of Time do not know what should and should not be done, their six senses gone.'
ramayana-3-29-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-16.translation: Having said this to Rama and knitting his brows, the night-roamer saw a great sala tree not far off.
ramayana-3-29-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-17.translation: Looking all around for a weapon in battle, he uprooted it, biting his lip.
ramayana-3-29-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-18.translation: Lifting it in both arms and roaring, the mighty one hurled it at Rama, saying, 'You are dead!'
ramayana-3-29-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-19.translation: Cutting it down with floods of arrows as it came, mighty Rama summoned fierce anger to kill Khara in battle.
ramayana-3-29-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-20.translation: Then Rama, sweating, his eye-corners red with anger, pierced Khara in battle with a thousand arrows.
ramayana-3-29-20.meaning: He struck Khara a thousand times.
ramayana-3-29-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-21.translation: From the gaps between the arrows much frothy blood flowed, like streams of water from a mountain spring.
ramayana-3-29-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-22.translation: Made unsteady by Rama's arrows in battle, Khara, maddened by the smell of blood, rushed at him quickly.
ramayana-3-29-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-23.translation: As he rushed furiously, bathed in blood, the skilled warrior Rama stepped back a little, step by step, quick in his moves.
ramayana-3-29-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-24.translation: Then, to kill Khara in battle, Rama took a fire-like arrow, like a second rod of Brahma.
ramayana-3-29-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-25.translation: The righteous one fitted that arrow, given by wise Indra, king of the gods, and released it at Khara.
ramayana-3-29-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-26.translation: That great arrow, released by Rama as he raised his bow, with a sound like a thunderclap, struck Khara in the chest.
ramayana-3-29-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-27.translation: Khara fell to the ground, burning in the fire of the arrow, like Andhaka burned up by Rudra in the White Forest.
ramayana-3-29-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-28.translation: Slain, Khara fell, like Vritra by the thunderbolt, Namuchi by foam, or Bala struck by Indra's lightning.
ramayana-3-29-28.meaning: He fell like the great demons of old.
ramayana-3-29-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-29.translation: Then all the royal sages and great seers gathered and, honouring Rama joyfully, said:
ramayana-3-29-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-30.translation: 'For this purpose mighty Indra, chastiser of Paka, destroyer of cities, came to Sharabhanga's holy hermitage.
ramayana-3-29-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-31.translation: You were brought to this region by the great seers through a plan, to kill these cruel demons of evil deeds.
ramayana-3-29-31.meaning: The sages had hoped Rama would come.
ramayana-3-29-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-32.translation: You have done this work for us, son of Dasharatha; the great seers will practise dharma happily in the Dandaka.'
ramayana-3-29-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-33.translation: Meanwhile the hero Lakshmana came out with Sita from the mountain stronghold and happily entered the hermitage.
ramayana-3-29-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-34.translation: Then victorious Rama, honoured by the great seers, entered the hermitage, saluted by Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-29-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-29-35.translation: Seeing her husband, slayer of enemies, bringer of happiness to the great seers, Sita was overjoyed and embraced him.
ramayana-3-29-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama kills Khara with an arrow given by Indra, and the sages rejoice that the Dandaka forest is safe.

ramayana-3-30-1.translation: Then Shurpanakha, seeing the fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds killed by Rama alone,
ramayana-3-30-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-2.translation: and seeing Dushana, Khara and Trishiras slain in battle, roared again a great roar like a thundercloud.
ramayana-3-30-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-3.translation: Seeing the deed done by Rama, very hard for others to do, she went, greatly alarmed, to Lanka, ruled by Ravana.
ramayana-3-30-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-4.translation: She saw Ravana, blazing with energy, on top of his palace, surrounded by ministers like Indra by the Maruts.
ramayana-3-30-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-5.translation: He sat on a golden, sun-bright high throne, like a great fire blazing on a golden altar,
ramayana-3-30-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-6.translation: invincible in battle by gods, gandharvas, beings and great seers, brave, like Death with open jaws,
ramayana-3-30-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-7.translation: bearing wounds from thunderbolts in the wars of gods and demons, his chest scarred by the tusks of Airavata,
ramayana-3-30-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-8.translation: with twenty arms and ten heads, splendid in his attire, broad-chested, heroic, marked with the signs of royalty,
ramayana-3-30-8.meaning: His famous ten heads and twenty arms.
ramayana-3-30-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-9.translation: shining like smooth beryl, with earrings of refined gold, fine arms, white teeth, a huge mouth, like a mountain,
ramayana-3-30-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-10.translation: his body struck hundreds of times by blows of Vishnu's discus in wars with the gods, and by all the gods' weapons,
ramayana-3-30-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-11.translation: one who stirs the unshakeable oceans, swift in action, hurler of mountain peaks and crusher of gods,
ramayana-3-30-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-12.translation: destroyer of dharma, violator of others' wives, user of all divine weapons, always obstructing sacrifices.
ramayana-3-30-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-13.translation: He had gone to the city of Bhogavati, defeated Vasuki and carried off Takshaka's beloved wife.
ramayana-3-30-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-14.translation: He had gone to Mount Kailasa, defeated Kubera and taken his chariot Pushpaka, which goes wherever one wishes.
ramayana-3-30-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-15.translation: In anger the mighty one destroyed the divine Chaitraratha forest, the lotus lake and the Nandana garden, the gardens of the gods.
ramayana-3-30-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-16.translation: Like a mountain peak, he blocked with his arms the noble moon and sun as they rose.
ramayana-3-30-16.meaning: He even blocked the sun and moon.
ramayana-3-30-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-17.translation: Steadfast, he once practised austerity in the great forest for ten thousand years and offered his heads to Brahma, the self-born.
ramayana-3-30-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-18.translation: He had no fear in battle of death from gods, danavas, gandharvas, pishachas, birds or serpents, except from a human.
ramayana-3-30-18.meaning: His boon did not protect him from humans.
ramayana-3-30-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described. This gap in Ravana's protection is why Vishnu is born as the human Rama.

ramayana-3-30-19.translation: The mighty one destroys the holy soma, praised with mantras by brahmins at sacrifices, in the vessels for offerings.
ramayana-3-30-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-20.translation: Ravana, destroyer of completed sacrifices, cruel, brahmin-killer, wicked in conduct, harsh, pitiless, intent on harming creatures, terror of all beings and all worlds:
ramayana-3-30-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-21.translation: the demoness saw her cruel, mighty brother, in divine clothes and ornaments, adorned with divine garlands, the lord of demons, delight of the line of Pulastya.
ramayana-3-30-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-30-22.translation: Faint with fear and confusion, showing herself disfigured by the great Rama, Shurpanakha, who used to move without fear, spoke very harsh words to him with his large blazing eyes.
ramayana-3-30-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 30: Shurpanakha flies to Lanka and finds Ravana, whose power and many misdeeds are described.

ramayana-3-31-1.translation: Then wretched and angry Shurpanakha spoke harsh words in the midst of the ministers to Ravana, who made the world cry:
ramayana-3-31-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

keywords.meaning: one who makes the world cry

ramayana-3-31-2.translation: 'Careless in pleasures, doing as you please, unrestrained, you do not notice the terrible danger that has arisen and must be noticed.
ramayana-3-31-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-3.translation: People do not respect a king attached to vulgar pleasures, ruled by desire and greedy, any more than the fire of a cremation ground.
ramayana-3-31-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-4.translation: A king who does not himself attend to his duties at the right time perishes along with his kingdom and those duties.
ramayana-3-31-4.meaning: A ruler must act in time.
ramayana-3-31-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-5.translation: People avoid from afar a king who has no spies, is hard to see and is not his own master, as elephants avoid river mud.
ramayana-3-31-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-6.translation: Kings who do not protect their realm and are not their own masters do not shine with prosperity, like mountains sunk in the sea.
ramayana-3-31-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-7.translation: Having made enemies of self-possessed gods, gandharvas and danavas, how will you remain king, fickle and without spies?
ramayana-3-31-7.meaning: You have many enemies and no watchfulness.
ramayana-3-31-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-8.translation: Kings whose spies, treasury and policy are not under their control are equal to common people, best of victors.
ramayana-3-31-8.meaning: A king must control intelligence and resources.
ramayana-3-31-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-9.translation: Because kings see all distant matters through spies, they are called 'long-sighted'.
ramayana-3-31-9.meaning: Good rulers know what happens far away.
ramayana-3-31-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-10.translation: I think you have no spies and are surrounded by common ministers, since you do not know your own people in Janasthana have been killed.
ramayana-3-31-10.meaning: You did not even know of the disaster.
ramayana-3-31-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-11.translation: Fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds have been killed by Rama alone, and Khara with Dushana.
ramayana-3-31-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-12.translation: Rama, tireless in deeds, has given the sages freedom from fear, made the Dandaka safe and attacked Janasthana.
ramayana-3-31-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-13.translation: But you, Ravana, are greedy, careless and dependent on others, since you do not notice the danger that has arisen in your own realm.
ramayana-3-31-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-14.translation: When a king is harsh, gives little, is careless, proud and deceitful, no creature runs to help him in disaster.
ramayana-3-31-14.meaning: Harsh rulers are abandoned in need.
ramayana-3-31-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-15.translation: Even his own people destroy, in disaster, a king who is too proud, unapproachable, self-important and angry.
ramayana-3-31-15.meaning: Pride makes enemies of one's own.
ramayana-3-31-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-16.translation: He who does not do his duties and does not fear what should be feared will soon fall from his kingdom, wretched, worth no more than grass.
ramayana-3-31-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-17.translation: Dry wood, clods of earth and even dust have their use, but kings fallen from their place have none.
ramayana-3-31-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-18.translation: Like a worn garment or a crushed garland, a king fallen from his kingdom, however able, is of no use.
ramayana-3-31-18.meaning: Power once lost is hard to regain.
ramayana-3-31-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-19.translation: But the king who is watchful, all-knowing, master of his senses, grateful and righteous lasts long.
ramayana-3-31-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed. A concise teaching on good leadership.

ramayana-3-31-20.translation: Though asleep with his eyes, he is awake with the eye of policy; and whose anger and favour are open is honoured by people.
ramayana-3-31-20.meaning: A good leader stays alert and transparent.
ramayana-3-31-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-21.translation: But you, Ravana, foolish-minded, lack these qualities, since your spies did not tell you of the great slaughter of the demons.
ramayana-3-31-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-22.translation: Despising others, attached to pleasures, not understanding the proper divisions of place and time, with a mind unfit to judge good and bad, your kingdom ruined, you will soon perish.'
ramayana-3-31-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-31-23.translation: Thus Ravana, lord of night-roamers, filled with wealth, pride and strength, considered with his mind the faults she had listed, and thought for a long time.
ramayana-3-31-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 31: Shurpanakha scolds Ravana for being a careless king who does not know that his army in Janasthana has been destroyed.

ramayana-3-32-1.translation: Then Ravana, angry, questioned angry Shurpanakha, who had spoken harsh words, in the midst of his ministers:
ramayana-3-32-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-2.translation: 'Who is Rama? What is his strength, his form, his valour? Why has he entered the very hard Dandaka forest?
ramayana-3-32-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-3.translation: What is Rama's weapon, by which the demons were killed, and Khara slain in battle, and Dushana and Trishiras?'
ramayana-3-32-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-4.translation: Thus addressed by the lord of demons, the demoness, faint with anger, began to describe Rama properly.
ramayana-3-32-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-5.translation: 'Long-armed, large-eyed, wearing bark and black deerskin, handsome as the god of love, is Rama, son of Dasharatha.
ramayana-3-32-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-6.translation: Drawing his gold-adorned bow, like Indra's rainbow, he shoots blazing iron arrows like very venomous snakes.
ramayana-3-32-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-7.translation: I did not see mighty Rama taking his terrible arrows, releasing them or drawing his bow in battle;
ramayana-3-32-7.meaning: He was too fast to see.
ramayana-3-32-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-8.translation: I only saw that army being destroyed by showers of arrows, like the best crop destroyed by Indra with showers of hail.
ramayana-3-32-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-9.translation: Fourteen thousand demons of terrible valour were killed by sharp arrows by him alone, on foot,
ramayana-3-32-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-10.translation: and in an hour and a half Khara with Dushana; he gave the sages freedom from fear and made the Dandaka safe.
ramayana-3-32-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-11.translation: I alone was somehow let go, humiliated by the great-souled Rama, self-aware, who shrank from killing a woman.
ramayana-3-32-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-12.translation: His brother, of great energy, equal in qualities and valour, devoted and loyal, is the valiant one named Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-32-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Ravana asks about Rama, and Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita.

ramayana-3-32-13.translation: Impatient of wrong, invincible, victorious, valiant, wise and strong, he is Rama's right arm, his very life walking outside him.
ramayana-3-32-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-14.translation: And Rama's lawful wife is the large-eyed, famous, lovely, slender-waisted Sita of Videha.
ramayana-3-32-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-15.translation: Neither goddess, gandharvi, yakshi nor kinnari, nor any such woman, have I seen on earth before.
ramayana-3-32-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-16.translation: He whose wife Sita would be, and whom she would joyfully embrace, would live more happily in all the worlds than even Indra.
ramayana-3-32-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-17.translation: She is of fine character, praised for her form, beyond compare in beauty on earth; she is a fitting wife for you, and you a fitting husband for her.
ramayana-3-32-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-18.translation: I was trying to bring that lovely-faced woman of beautiful form to you as your wife.
ramayana-3-32-18.meaning: She claimed she meant Sita for Ravana.
ramayana-3-32-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife. Shurpanakha twists the story to stir Ravana's desire.

ramayana-3-32-19.translation: Seeing Sita today, with her face like the full moon, you will fall under the arrows of the god of love.
ramayana-3-32-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-20.translation: If you wish her as your wife, quickly set forth your right foot here for victory.
ramayana-3-32-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-21.translation: And do a kindness to those demons, lord of demons, by killing that cruel Rama who lives in the hermitage.
ramayana-3-32-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-22.translation: Having killed him and the great warrior Lakshmana with sharp arrows, you will enjoy Sita happily, her protector slain.
ramayana-3-32-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-23.translation: If my words please you, lord of demons, act on them without hesitation.
ramayana-3-32-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-32-24.translation: Having heard that the night-roamers of Janasthana were killed by Rama with straight-flying arrows, and knowing Khara and Dushana slain, you should act today.'
ramayana-3-32-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 32: Shurpanakha describes Rama, Lakshmana and Sita's beauty, urging Ravana to take Sita as his wife.

ramayana-3-33-1.translation: Hearing Shurpanakha's hair-raising words, Ravana dismissed his ministers and, having decided what to do, departed.
ramayana-3-33-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-2.translation: Considering the matter, understanding it properly and weighing the strengths and weaknesses of its faults and merits,
ramayana-3-33-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-3.translation: having resolved 'This must be done', firm of mind, he went to the lovely chariot house.
ramayana-3-33-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-4.translation: Going to the chariot house secretly, the lord of demons ordered his charioteer: 'Yoke the chariot.'
ramayana-3-33-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-5.translation: Thus told, the quick charioteer at once yoked his favourite, excellent chariot.
ramayana-3-33-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-6.translation: Mounting the golden chariot that went where he wished, adorned with jewels and drawn by goblin-faced donkeys decked with gold,
ramayana-3-33-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-7.translation: the glorious lord of demons, younger brother of Kubera, went with a sound like a thundercloud toward the ocean, lord of rivers.
ramayana-3-33-7.meaning: He set off across the sea.
ramayana-3-33-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-8.translation: Ten-faced, with white yak-tail fans and a white parasol, shining like smooth beryl, adorned with refined gold,
ramayana-3-33-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-9.translation: ten-faced, twenty-armed, splendidly dressed, enemy of the gods and killer of great sages, like a ten-peaked king of mountains,
ramayana-3-33-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-10.translation: the lord of demons shone in his wish-going chariot like a cloud in the sky with lightning flashes and cranes.
ramayana-3-33-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-11.translation: The mighty one looked down on the seacoast with its mountains, strewn with thousands of trees bearing many flowers and fruits,
ramayana-3-33-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-12.translation: surrounded on all sides by lotus ponds with cool, auspicious water and by large hermitages with altars,
ramayana-3-33-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-13.translation: crowded with plantain and adhaki, adorned with coconut palms, with sala, palm, tamala and flowering trees,
ramayana-3-33-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-14.translation: graced by great seers of very restrained diet, and by thousands of nagas, suparnas, gandharvas and kinnaras,
ramayana-3-33-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-15.translation: adorned with perfected beings who had conquered desire, celestial singers, and Aja, Vaikhanasa, Masha, Valakhilya and Marichipa sages,
ramayana-3-33-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-16.translation: filled with thousands of apsaras of divine form, wearing divine ornaments and garlands, skilled in play and love,
ramayana-3-33-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-17.translation: frequented by the glorious wives of the gods and visited by hosts of gods and danavas who feed on nectar,
ramayana-3-33-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-18.translation: scattered with swans, herons and frogs, echoing with cranes, lovely, with beryl stones, glossy with the ocean's brilliance.
ramayana-3-33-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-19.translation: All around were large white celestial chariots adorned with divine garlands, filled with music and song.
ramayana-3-33-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-20.translation: Kubera's younger brother saw the wish-going chariots of those who had won worlds by austerity, and gandharvas and apsaras.
ramayana-3-33-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-21.translation: He saw thousands of gentle sandal forests, with resin-rich roots, delightful to the nose,
ramayana-3-33-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-22.translation: forests and groves of the finest aloe wood, and of takkola trees with fragrant fruits,
ramayana-3-33-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-23.translation: flowers of tamala, shrubs of pepper, and heaps of pearls drying on the shore,
ramayana-3-33-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-24.translation: beds of conch shells, heaps of coral, and mountains of gold and silver everywhere,
ramayana-3-33-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-25.translation: charming waterfalls and clear lakes, cities full of wealth and grain and filled with jewels among women,
ramayana-3-33-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-26.translation: crowded with elephants, horses and chariots. He saw the shore of the king of rivers, level everywhere, smooth, with soft breezes,
ramayana-3-33-26.meaning: He looked down at all this.
ramayana-3-33-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-27.translation: like heaven. There he saw a banyan like a cloud, surrounded by sages,
ramayana-3-33-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-28.translation: whose branches spread a hundred yojanas all around; to whose branch mighty Garuda once came, carrying an elephant and a huge tortoise to eat.
ramayana-3-33-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-29.translation: Suddenly the mighty Suparna, best of birds, broke that leafy branch with his weight.
ramayana-3-33-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-30.translation: On it were gathered great seers: Vaikhanasas, Mashas, Valakhilyas, Marichipas, Ajas and Dhumras.
ramayana-3-33-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-31.translation: Out of compassion for them, Garuda quickly carried away that hundred-yojana branch, along with the elephant and the tortoise.
ramayana-3-33-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-32.translation: The righteous best of birds ate that flesh with one foot, destroyed the land of the Nishadas with the branch, and felt boundless joy at freeing the great sages.
ramayana-3-33-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-33.translation: With that very joy his strength doubled, and the wise one resolved to bring back the nectar of immortality.
ramayana-3-33-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-34.translation: Breaking the iron nets and splitting the excellent jewelled house, he carried off the guarded nectar from great Indra's palace.
ramayana-3-33-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-35.translation: Kubera's younger brother saw that banyan named Subhadra, frequented by hosts of great seers and bearing the marks Garuda made.
ramayana-3-33-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-36.translation: Going to the far shore of the ocean, lord of rivers, he saw a hermitage in a secluded, holy, lovely part of the forest.
ramayana-3-33-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-37.translation: There he saw the demon named Maricha, wearing black deerskin, matted hair and bark, restrained in diet.
ramayana-3-33-37.meaning: He found Maricha living as an ascetic.
ramayana-3-33-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-33-38.translation: Ravana met that demon in the proper way, and then the skilled speaker said these words:
ramayana-3-33-38.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 33: Ravana secretly sets out in his flying chariot across the sea, passing the great banyan of Garuda's legend, and reaches the hermitage of the demon Maricha.

ramayana-3-34-1.translation: 'Maricha, dear one, listen to what I say. I am in distress, and you are my highest refuge in distress.
ramayana-3-34-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-2.translation: You know Janasthana, where my brother Khara, mighty-armed Dushana and my sister Shurpanakha lived,
ramayana-3-34-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-3.translation: and the mighty flesh-eating demon Trishiras, and many other brave night-roamers who never miss their mark.
ramayana-3-34-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-4.translation: They lived there by my order, troubling the sages who follow dharma in the great forest.
ramayana-3-34-4.meaning: They lived there on his command.
ramayana-3-34-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-5.translation: Fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds, brave, sure of aim, following Khara's will,
ramayana-3-34-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-6.translation: these mighty ones living in Janasthana, gathered and fully prepared, met Rama in battle.
ramayana-3-34-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-7.translation: Rama, enraged at the head of battle, without saying anything harsh, put his bow to work with arrows,
ramayana-3-34-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-8.translation: and fourteen thousand demons of terrible deeds were killed with sharp arrows by a man on foot.
ramayana-3-34-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-9.translation: Khara was killed in battle and Dushana brought down; having killed Trishiras too, he made the Dandaka free of fear.
ramayana-3-34-9.meaning: The forest is now safe from demons.
ramayana-3-34-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-10.translation: Driven out by his angry father with his wife, his life nearly spent, that Rama, disgrace to the warrior class, has destroyed that army.
ramayana-3-34-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-11.translation: He is without virtue, harsh, fierce, foolish, greedy, without self-control; he has abandoned dharma, is unrighteous and bent on harming creatures.
ramayana-3-34-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita. Ravana's description is the opposite of the truth; Maricha corrects him in the next chapter.

ramayana-3-34-12.translation: Without any enmity, relying only on his strength, he disfigured my sister in the forest by cutting off her ears and nose.
ramayana-3-34-12.meaning: He told only part of the story.
ramayana-3-34-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-13.translation: I will bravely carry off his wife Sita, like a daughter of the gods, from Janasthana; be my helper in this.
ramayana-3-34-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-14.translation: With you as my helper at my side, mighty one, and my brothers, I do not think about all the gods in battle.
ramayana-3-34-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-15.translation: So be my helper, for you are able, demon; there is none equal to you in valour, war and pride.
ramayana-3-34-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-16.translation: For this I have come to you, night-roamer. Hear what you must do to help, at my word.
ramayana-3-34-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-17.translation: Become a golden deer, spotted with silver drops, and roam in front of Sita in Rama's hermitage.
ramayana-3-34-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-18.translation: Seeing you in the form of a deer, Sita will without doubt tell her husband and Lakshmana, "Catch it!"
ramayana-3-34-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-19.translation: Then, when the two are gone and the place is empty, I will carry off Sita at my ease, unhindered, as Rahu takes the moonlight.
ramayana-3-34-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.
